title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23, accompanied by the Heritage Orchestra, Flames Collective choir and her band.
body:
RAYE will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23, accompanied by the Heritage Orchestra, Flames Collective choir and her band. The one-night show is titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* and will feature new orchestral arrangements of the songs. It brings her back to the venue where she first presented her music with an orchestra in 2023. This time, however, the album was written with several of those musical elements already in place.

Released on March 27, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* unfolds across four seasons, with the songs gradually moving from darkness toward hope. Its arrangements draw on jazz, soul, big-band music and orchestral writing. Hans Zimmer appears on "Click Clack Symphony.", while the London Symphony Orchestra and Flames Collective also contributed to the record. The music was not conceived as a collection of stripped-back pop songs awaiting orchestral accompaniment. Those sounds are already part of the recordings, and the October concert will put them in the hands of a different ensemble.

The Royal Albert Hall hosted her first *My 21st Century Symphony* concert three years ago, with a 50-piece orchestra and choir performing music from *My 21st Century Blues*. The performance was filmed as *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*, which went on to receive a Grammy nomination for Best Music Film. She brought the symphonic show to the O2 in 2024, again working with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective. The October concert will revisit that collaboration with an entirely different album.

RAYE has already shared an example of the new material in an orchestral setting. Released alongside the concert announcement, "I Will Overcome. (Live at Abbey Road Studios)" was recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra. It is a studio performance, not footage from the upcoming concert, and the players are not the same ensemble booked for the Royal Albert Hall. The song is the first full-length track on the album after its brief introduction, making it an appropriate place to hear how the new arrangements might develop.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

The album has had a successful year beyond the concert stage. It became RAYE's first UK No. 1 album in April, and the single "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" has continued to find listeners since its release last year. On the record, that hit appears well into the second half, followed by several quieter pieces. The Royal Albert Hall program will include it, but the decision to perform the album in its original sequence means those later songs will be heard as part of the same performance.

The announcement also arrives after a busy period of touring. RAYE played six sold-out concerts at London's O2 earlier this year and took the album on a North American tour before joining Bruno Mars for stadium dates. She also performed "I Will Overcome." at the MTV Video Music Awards in September. The Abbey Road recording gives that song another interpretation, with a full orchestra rather than the arrangement audiences heard during her arena concerts.

One of the album's less conventional choices is its ending. The final track, "Fin.", lasts six minutes and 27 seconds and begins by addressing the listener who has made it through the whole record. In a concert drawn from across an artist's catalog, that farewell might lose the songs that give it meaning. At the Royal Albert Hall, RAYE plans to perform the entire album in order. The final song will follow the rest of the story, ending with a thank-you to the person who has listened all the way through.
